audit_notes: Parameter check. The claimed effective net longwave loss of 45 W/m2 per wall area is optimistic: a flat vertical emitter sees half sky and half hot ground (ground ~50-60 C by day), so its net longwave exchange is only ~5-20 W/m2; 45-degree facets see ~0.85 sky, but in a corrugation they also see each other and part of the ground-facing facets; I estimate 30 W/m2 (including eps~0.95). Upward-tilted facets also collect more beam and diffuse sun than a vertical wall, which offsets part of the self-shading; I set the effective absorptance (referred to the vertical-wall irradiance) to 0.15 instead of 0.12. Baseline: flat wall with aged cool paint: absorptance 0.32, net longwave 0.9*20 = 18 W/m2. Dimensionless: facet sky view factor (1+cos(45deg))/2 = 0.85; Biot envelope 0.026. Simulation coefficient: effective sol-air excess of the design (0.15*300-30)/20 = 0.75 K vs baseline (96-18)/20 = 3.9 K. Model: steady 1D conduction, analytical. Expected gain ~19% (west wall). Mechanical: corrugated metal/fibre-cement panels are standard; upward facets collect dust and bird droppings, which is the main durability risk. Audit passed.
